item.title: Advancing towards a Responsible and Resilient Digital Future
item.content:encoded:
Digital technologies like AI and blockchain create significant value but also introduce serious challenges including algorithmic bias, privacy violations, and workforce disruption. The special issue seeks research on information systems that are simultaneously responsible—fair, transparent, ethical, and accountable—and resilient, capable of withstanding disruptions while delivering sustained value.

While responsibility and resilience in digital systems are interdependent, they have largely evolved as separate research streams. Information systems scholars are uniquely positioned to examine human–technology interaction, value realization from digital investments, and how governance shapes digital outcomes, particularly for vulnerable populations. The special issue invites theoretically grounded, methodologically rigorous research using diverse methods including conceptual work, surveys, experiments, and design science approaches.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence, Affective Computing and Video Analytics for Intelligent Information Systems
item.content:encoded:
Luigi Gallo, Pegaso University

Andrea Generosi, Pegaso University

Valerio De Luca, Pegaso University

Maura Mengoni, Marche Polytechnic University

Lucio Tommaso De Paolis, University of Salento

Josef Spjut, Nvidia

This special issue addresses the convergence of video analytics and affective computing in intelligent information systems. With the rapid growth of video data across surveillance, retail, healthcare, and social platforms, combined with advances in deep learning and multimodal models, there is an opportunity to harness emotional and social signals from visual data to enhance decision-making systems. The issue seeks research that bridges computer vision, sentiment detection, and system design to create human-centered, explainable solutions.

The call welcomes original research, surveys, and perspectives on topics ranging from scalable video understanding and real-time emotion detection to multimodal analysis combining vision, audio, and text. Particular interest lies in streaming-native AI architectures, video-language models, edge/cloud systems, and techniques addressing fairness, privacy, and compliance. Applications span healthcare, finance, education, and smart environments, with emphasis on practical implementation at scale.

item.title: Digital Technologies for Combating Unethical Labour Practices and Promoting Human Rights
item.content:encoded:
Unethical labour practices, including modern slavery, affect approximately 50 million people worldwide and are expected to worsen due to regional conflicts and restrictive migration policies. Although digital technologies such as blockchain, AI, and cloud computing show promise in addressing these issues, research examining their specific applications remains limited. This special issue seeks to bridge this gap by exploring how digital technologies can be leveraged theoretically and empirically to monitor, detect, report, and remediate unethical labour practices.

The call invites original, theory-driven research using diverse methodologies including theoretical frameworks, case studies, surveys, and literature reviews. Submissions should identify specific digital technologies and provide nuanced insights into how they can combat labour exploitation and support human rights. Particularly encouraged are studies that challenge existing paradigms, explore underexamined dimensions, or offer innovative perspectives that inform policymakers and practitioners on leveraging technology for meaningful change.

item.title: From Adoption to Impact: Post-Adoption, Value Realization, and Societal Transformation of ICT and AI
item.content:encoded:
This special issue investigates how organizations and society create and realize value from ICT and AI technologies beyond their initial adoption phase. While prior research has focused extensively on adoption decisions, this collection addresses understudied post-adoption dynamics including continuance, adaptation, and routinization. The issue recognizes that technology adoption alone does not guarantee organizational or societal benefits, necessitating deeper understanding of how sustained technology use generates value and drives transformation.

The special issue welcomes empirical, theoretical, experimental, design science, and review-based research examining post-adoption phenomena, value realization, and transformation at individual, organizational, and societal levels. It seeks to balance exploration of positive impacts with critical examination of risks and challenges, including ethical concerns, digital inequality, cybersecurity threats, and unintended consequences of widespread ICT and AI deployment. Novel perspectives on early-stage adoption are also welcome when they offer new theoretical insights or address emerging technologies.

item.title: Keeping Humans in the Loop in the AI-Driven Future of Information Security
item.content:encoded:
As artificial intelligence increasingly shapes both offensive and defensive cybersecurity, this special issue emphasizes the continuing importance of human judgment and involvement in security systems. The call recognizes that while AI tools are becoming essential for threat detection and response, humans remain fundamental to effective security practice. The special issue seeks research that maintains focus on how humans can effectively collaborate with AI-based systems rather than being replaced by them.

The special issue invites behavioral and design science research exploring how to balance AI advancement with meaningful human participation in security. Beyond traditional topics like security compliance and training, the call particularly welcomes studies on neurosecurity approaches, AI-enabled behavioral interventions, human-AI collaboration in security decisions, and the security implications of generative AI. The work should emphasize practical applications, such as improving security awareness or detecting threats through behavioral analysis, rather than purely technical solutions.
